# Claim

Indus building groups negotiated changes to their houses while preserving shared routes and services. The repeated unit of urban coordination was the agreement connecting adjacent groups through streets, drains and entrances. Districts could grow, subdivide or change orientation while that agreement continued.

# Why we think this

The [comparative study](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/REPORT.md) connects Banawali's deliberate replanning, Kanmer's infill with retained alignment, Farmana's local encroachments and the wall and hydraulic sequences at Dholavira and Lothal. These sequences support different scales of intervention. Their institutional cause remains a conjecture. The [methods](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/METHODS.md) distinguish a negotiated arrangement from uniform supervision and independent convergence.

# Predictions

| ID | Prediction | New data and pass rule | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Shared routes persist more often than internal plot partitions across rebuilding | At least 12 independently phase-joined episodes from at least four towns. Freeze common-route and plot-wall coding blind to inscriptions. The retained fraction differs by at least 0.25 and its town-cluster interval excludes zero. | untested |
| P2 | Neighbouring groups retain local construction differences while joining a shared repair | At least six new, directly joined drain or street repairs in three towns. Component-level material or dimensional differences persist across at least four repairs, with the connected route demonstrably usable. | untested |
| P3 | Repair timing groups by connected infrastructure more strongly than by proximity alone | Independently model construction boundaries; compare connection-based and distance-only models on entirely withheld episode groups. The former improves the prespecified predictive score with leave-one-town-out stability. Pilot power and scoring family must be frozen before confirmation. | untested |

P1 and P2 share evidence and receive one joint update. If both pass and independent review retains the phase and hydraulic joins, credence becomes 0.70. If P1 fails with adequate sensitivity to a 0.25 difference, credence becomes 0.25. P3 is a deciding follow-up and cannot be combined as independent evidence when it reuses those episodes.

# Kill condition

Abandon the claim if new phase-keyed surveys show that supposed retained shared routes are composite-plan or restoration artifacts, or if a powered comparison finds a common settlement-wide rebuilding sequence and uniform component choices that account for the claimed local negotiation. A lack of comparable phases postpones the test.

# Record

24 October 2026: proposed from examined literature. The attached [versioned shots output](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/bench-shots-synthetic-v1.json) tests generated workflow guards only. It supplies no archaeological score. No confirmation material was opened. The [prospective design](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/TEST-DESIGN.md) specifies the acquisition and power gates before a real registered round.

# Claim

Indus sealings recorded responsibility at handovers between urban groups. Their recurring legends connected institutions across districts and towns, while the particular stamp identified an authorising holder. The relevant architectural settings were controlled passages, storage access and points where goods changed custody.

# Evidence and extension

The project has physical fastening evidence from Lothal and repeated texts carried by different stamps across sites. The [new study](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/REPORT.md) adds the distinction between a use context, a workshop, a discarded assemblage and a building associated only by a reused label. A sealing's fastening trace supports closure or attachment; responsibility and institutional handover remain the proposed function. No sound value or sign gloss follows from this claim.

# Predictions

| ID | Prediction | New data and pass rule | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Used sealings are enriched at independently identified controlled handovers | New primary-use deposits from at least four towns and 20 matched context pairs. Match phase, sampled sediment, recovery and preservation. A conditional model gives an odds ratio of at least 2 with its cluster interval above 1, retaining direction when any town is omitted. | untested |
| P2 | Closing text units recur across handover settings more than manufacture style does | Freeze units on discovery only. Keep physical aliases, impressions of one stamp and copied production series together. Compare new districts and towns while withholding their identities. The joint predictive model exceeds declared within-period rearrangements and its gain survives influence checks. | untested |
| P3 | The architectural relation survives use and discard coding | Independently code fastening, breakage and redeposition. P1's association remains in the primary-use subset and is not generated entirely by secondary dumps. | untested |

All predictions share a joint update. P1 and P3 passing moves credence to 0.50. P2 also passing on new material moves it to 0.65. A powered failure of P1 and P3 moves it to 0.10. These are proposed update rules; the pilot must fix sample sufficiency and scoring before a real confirmation round.

# Kill condition

Abandon the handover claim if adequately sampled, primary-use contexts show that the material is explained by household possession or workshop disposal and does not predict independently coded custody changes. Recurring text alone cannot rescue a failed physical-use prediction.

# Record

24 October 2026: proposed. Current Lothal and Harappa objects are already examined, and the site, motif and object-type statistic families are spent. The [attached shots run](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/bench-shots-synthetic-v1.json) has `synthetic: true`; its guard checks are procedural evidence only. See [TEST-DESIGN](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/TEST-DESIGN.md).

# Claim

Harappa's repeated tablet series recorded obligations or entitlements for work on shared infrastructure. The repeated descriptor identified a work group or service and the varying stroke group identified an obligation class. Production batches made comparable records available to several participants.

# Why take this shot

Serial production, recurring faces and varying stroke groups make a repeatable administrative instrument plausible. Repeated urban maintenance provides a concrete activity that needed coordination. Their connection is the long shot. The [source record](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/modules/inscriptions/RESEARCH.md) gives manufacturing and secondary-discard contexts; none independently identifies a labour account. The claim adds a specific institutional referent to C-0005 and carries a lower credence than the generic token model.

# Predictions

| ID | Prediction | New data and pass rule | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Newly recovered tablet series occur in primary contexts associated with shared works | In a new sample with at least 20 matched context pairs and a preregistered useful effect, tablet occurrence predicts a directly evidenced maintenance or provisioning context after controls for domestic storage, craft production and trade. Pass requires conditional odds ratio at least 2 and a cluster interval above 1. | untested |
| P2 | Varying stroke groups covary with independently measured work or provision classes | Freeze the classes from physical evidence without reading inscriptions. A model using the frozen face units predicts those classes better than within-frequency rearrangements, with component influence checks and transfer to a new excavation block. | untested |
| P3 | Material associations distinguish shared work from ordinary container labelling | New wear, residues, discard sequences or direct associations supply an independent distinction between labour provisioning and goods storage. The decision rule must be established from a blinded pilot and frozen before confirmation. | untested |

These are acquisition targets, not a ready-to-run confirmation protocol. P1 alone moves credence to 0.18. P1 and P2 passing with P3's independent distinction moves it to 0.35. A powered failure of P1 or P2 moves it to 0.03. All overlapping observations receive one joint update.

# Kill condition

Abandon this specific labour reading if a new, independently coded sample ties the varying series to stored goods or another activity that explains their variation and defeats the shared-work prediction, or if a sufficiently powered prospective test yields no useful association. Failure leaves the broader proposition of serial administrative tablets available for separate tests.

# Record

24 October 2026: long-shot proposal. No sign meaning is scored or established. The [versioned synthetic shots result](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/bench-shots-synthetic-v1.json) checks the future workflow. The current corpus and published contexts are exposed, and no confirmation half was opened. See the common [test design](../../experiments/2026-10-24-urban-form-and-inscription-ecology/TEST-DESIGN.md).
